subjective.question: What do we mean by cognitive process?
subjective.answer: Cognitive process is the mental process of knowing, including aspects such as awareness, perception, reasoning, and judgment.

subjective.question: List any three normative models of Choice Phase of decision making process.
subjective.answer: The Choice Phase: A course of action is selected out of the available alternatives as devised in the design phase. Typical activities include: 1. Get information 2. Final evaluation

subjective.question: Sensitivity analysis
DSS are used to take help in Semi structured decisions. What does DSS use as support in order to facilitate Semi Structured Decision making?
subjective.answer: A DSS assists management decision making by combining data, sophisticated analytical models and user-friendly software into a single powerful system that can support semi-structured or unstructured decision making. Unstructured problems are novel, non-routine and have no predefined algorithms or solutions. DSS combine data with models to produce various alternative scenarios that can be used for making choices. In large organizations decision making is inherently a group process, and DSS can be designed to facilitate group decision making.

subjective.question: Write down any two characteristics of structured decisions.
subjective.answer: Any two of the following: 1. Structured decisions are repetitive and routine in nature, i.e. the same type of decision is made again and again. 2. The procedures (rules/steps) to follow when such a decision is needed can be specified in advance. 3. They involve a definite, pre-defined procedure for handling them, so that a consistent solution is obtained every time; they are mostly made at the operational level of the organization.

subjective.question: For each of the given below statements, identify the organizational model of decision making.

A model which is not rational, in which decisions are made on accidental basis. 2. A model in which managers attempt to gather more administrative and financial power. 3. A model in which organization does not choose and decide rational sense but uses a specific set of SOP.
subjective.answer: 1. Garbage Can Model — decisions are not rational; they are made on an accidental basis, as outcomes of streams of problems, solutions and participants coming together by chance.

subjective.question: Political Model — managers attempt to gather more administrative and financial power, and decisions reflect the interests and bargaining of powerful groups/individuals.
Bureaucratic Model — the organization does not choose and decide in a rational sense but uses a specific set of SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures).

Let us consider an organization XYZ in which all of the managers who are responsible for decision making are geographically dispersed or they are not available at one place at the same time, but still it is required to take combined and efficient decisions; identify that which type of system will help in efficient decision making in this case? Also list at least three characteristics of this system.
subjective.answer: The system is a Group Decision Support System (GDSS) — a type of DSS specially designed to support a group of decision makers working together, instead of a single individual. Characteristics (any three): 1. It supports group decision making even when the members are at different places and/or available at different times (same time/same place, same time/different place, different time/different place). 2. It provides electronic communication facilities such as e-mail/messaging, video conferencing and shared screens/documents, so dispersed managers can exchange ideas and data. 3. It is a combination of special software, hardware (decision room/network setup) and procedures designed to support and improve group decisions. 4. It allows parallel and anonymous input of ideas, which reduces the dominance of a few members and improves the quality of decisions. 5. It supports structured group activities such as electronic brainstorming, idea organization, voting and ranking of alternatives.

subjective.question: Identify the basic function and responsibilities of a system analyst.
subjective.answer: A person who has a detailed knowledge of computers and system design — his basic function is said to be system analyst. Systems analysts work as a link between business people and computer programmers. Functions of system analysis: at least one person should have a detailed knowledge of: 1. The organization 2. How the current system operates 3. Information needs of the system 4. Defects in the existing system

subjective.question: What do you understand by ERD? Define briefly.
subjective.answer: A diagrammatical tool used in system design is ERD (Entity Relationship Diagram). ERD indicates simple relationships. These relationships can be read as follows: 1. One department has one supervisor. 2. A department may have more than one employees. Or: 1. An employee may be in more than one departments. 2. An employee may not be working on any project, but a project must have at least one employee working on it.

subjective.question: What do you understand by system design and identify the steps it includes.
subjective.answer: System design includes the desired features and operations in detail, including screen layouts, business rules, process diagrams and other documentation. It involves converting the informational, functional, and network requirements identified during the initiation and planning phases into unified design specifications. Steps included in system design are given below: 1. Formulation of strategic requirements 2. Organizational & job design 3. Elicitation of detailed requirements 4. Design of the information flow 5. Design of database 6. Design of user interface 7. Physical design 8. Design of hardware & software platform

subjective.question: Why Software development life cycle is considered as an on-going process?
subjective.answer: The Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) is considered an on-going (cyclic) process because a system is never truly finished. After implementation, the system enters the maintenance phase, where errors are corrected and new requirements keep arising due to changes in the business environment, technology and user needs. Each change or enhancement again passes through the same phases — analysis, design, development and implementation — so the cycle keeps repeating throughout the entire life of the system.

subjective.question: Suppose a ready made garment manufacturing factory decides to develop a financial application for its finance department. In your opinion, what aspects or criterion should be considered for this software product to be technically feasible? Mention any three of them.
subjective.answer: Technical feasibility examines whether the proposed software can be developed and implemented with the available technology. Any three aspects/criteria: 1. Availability of technology: whether the required hardware and software technology (e.g. computers, database and development tools) exists and can be acquired by the factory. 2. Availability of technical expertise: whether skilled staff are available (or can be hired/trained) to develop, operate and maintain the financial application. 3. Compatibility with the existing system: whether the new application can be integrated with the factory's existing hardware, software and procedures without major disruption. (Other valid points: whether the technology is mature and reliable, and whether required performance/response time can be achieved.)

subjective.question: Draw the Data Flow Diagram for student enrollment process of a Distance Learning University. The student enrollment process works as follow: - The student sends an application form containing his/her personal details and his/her desired course. - The university checks the course availability and necessary academic qualifications of the student. - If the course is available, the student will be enrolled in the course and the university confirms the enrollment by sending a confirmation letter to the student. - If the course is unavailable, the student will be sent a rejection letter.
subjective.answer: The DFD is described below (draw it using standard symbols: square = external entity, circle/rounded box = process, open-ended rectangle = data store, arrow = data flow). External Entity: Student. Process 1.0 — Check Course Availability & Qualifications: receives the Application Form from the Student; checks the desired course against the Courses data store and the student's academic qualifications. Process 2.0 — Enroll Student: if the course is available and the student qualifies, enrolls the student and records the enrollment in the Student Enrollment data store. Data Stores: D1 Courses (course availability record); D2 Student Enrollment (enrolled students record). Data Flows: - Student → Process 1.0: Application Form (personal details + desired course) - Process 1.0 ↔ D1 Courses: course availability information - Process 1.0 → Process 2.0: approved application - Process 2.0 → D2 Student Enrollment: enrollment record - Process 2.0 → Student: Confirmation Letter (on successful enrollment) - Process 1.0 → Student: Rejection Letter (if the course is unavailable)

subjective.question: Define an information system and list its basic components.
subjective.answer: An information system is a set of interrelated components that collect (input), process, store and distribute information to support decision making, coordination and control in an organization. Basic components: 1. Hardware — the physical equipment (computers, printers, etc.) 2. Software — the programs that process the data 3. Data — the raw facts stored and processed by the system 4. Procedures — the defined set of instructions/rules for using the system 5. People — the users and specialists who operate and use the system

subjective.question: Differentiate between data and information.
subjective.answer: Data is the raw, unprocessed facts and figures (e.g. numbers, names, marks obtained by students) which have no meaning on their own. Information is the processed/organized form of data that is meaningful and useful for decision making (e.g. the merit list or result summary prepared from students' marks). In short, data is the input to a system and information is its useful output.

subjective.question: Differentiate between an open system and a closed system.
subjective.answer: An open system interacts with its environment: it takes inputs from the environment and depends on external resources and data (e.g. market information) for decision making. A closed system does not interact with its environment; it depends on internal resources and data for decision making rather than the external environment. In practice, most real-world systems are relatively open systems.

subjective.question: What are primary, secondary and tertiary sources of information? Give one example of each.
subjective.answer: Primary sources present information in its original form, neither interpreted nor condensed nor evaluated by other writers — e.g. original research reports, diaries, interviews, official records. Secondary sources present information that has been interpreted, condensed or evaluated from primary sources — e.g. textbooks, review articles, commentaries. Tertiary sources contain information in which the information from secondary sources has been digested — reformatted and condensed into a convenient, easy-to-read form, and they list primary and secondary resources of a subject area — e.g. indexes, bibliographies, encyclopedias and directories.

subjective.question: List and briefly explain the phases of the decision making process.
subjective.answer: The decision making process (Simon's model) consists of the following phases: 1. Intelligence — searching the environment for conditions calling for a decision; the problem is identified and defined. 2. Design — inventing, developing and analyzing possible courses of action (alternatives). 3. Choice — selecting a particular course of action from the available alternatives. 4. Implementation — putting the selected course of action into practice. 5. Monitoring — evaluating the outcome of the implemented decision and taking corrective action if required.

subjective.question: Differentiate between structured, semi-structured and unstructured decisions.
subjective.answer: Structured decisions are repetitive and routine; the procedures to follow can be specified in advance, e.g. inventory re-ordering — they are supported by TPS/MIS. Semi-structured decisions are those where only some phases of the decision process are structured; they combine standard procedures with the manager's judgment, e.g. deciding a marketing budget — they are supported by DSS. Unstructured decisions are novel, non-routine and important; there may be several 'right' answers and no precise/cut-and-dried method to get a right answer, e.g. launching a new product line — they are made mostly at the strategic level and supported by ESS/DSS.

subjective.question: Differentiate between TPS, MIS and DSS.
subjective.answer: TPS (Transaction Processing System) records and processes the routine day-to-day business transactions (e.g. sales, payroll) and serves the operational level of the organization. MIS (Management Information System) converts TPS data into summarized, routine reports (e.g. monthly sales reports) that help middle managers in monitoring and controlling the business; it supports structured decisions. DSS (Decision Support System) combines data, sophisticated analytical models and user-friendly software to help managers make semi-structured and unstructured decisions, e.g. through what-if analysis.

subjective.question: Name the three levels of management and state the type of decisions/information required at each level.
subjective.answer: 1. Operational level — supervisors/foremen; they make structured, day-to-day decisions and need detailed, current, internal information (supported by TPS). 2. Managerial (tactical) level — middle managers; they make semi-structured decisions and need summarized periodic reports for monitoring and control (supported by MIS/DSS). 3. Strategic level — top management; they make unstructured, long-term decisions such as formulation of new products and identifying new opportunities, and need summarized internal plus external information (supported by ESS).

subjective.question: What is organizational culture? How does it affect the information systems of an organization?
subjective.answer: Organizational culture is the specific collection of values and norms that are shared by people and groups in an organization and that control the way they interact with each other and with stakeholders outside the organization. It affects information systems because a new system must fit the culture of the organization: if the system conflicts with the shared values, work habits and power structure of the employees, they may resist or reject it, causing system failure; a culture that supports sharing and openness, on the other hand, makes system adoption and use more successful.

subjective.question: Compare the Waterfall model and the Spiral model of system development.
subjective.answer: Waterfall model: development proceeds in a linear, sequential manner — each phase (analysis, design, coding, testing, maintenance) is completed fully before the next begins; it is simple but rigid, and going back to a previous phase is difficult. Spiral model: development is a series of short waterfall cycles, each producing an early prototype representing a part of the entire project; it is iterative and risk-driven, allowing user feedback and changes at every cycle, but it is more complex and costly to manage.

subjective.question: Differentiate CBIS from manual information systems.
subjective.answer: In manual environment, the concept of transformation was difficult to apply, since input of data into records was by itself the output which also included simple computations. Concept of control mechanism grew stronger as computerized information systems emerged. CBIS is an Information System that uses computer & telecommunications technology to perform its intended tasks. In CBIS, Information technology (IT) becomes a subset of the Information system.

subjective.question: What should be the basic characteristics of paper free environment?
subjective.answer: • Information overload enhances paper work. • Maintenance of records in hard form has always proven to be a cumbersome task. • An IS/CBIS should be efficient enough to properly manage documents electronically. • Customer orders are met through Virtual Private Networks and intranets. • Payments are made through Electronic payment system. • Report generation and record analysis gets convenient and easy.

subjective.question: Discuss components of a system.
subjective.answer: Following are the important components of the system: • Input elements — Raw data input to the computer system • Process — Computation, analysis, application of any model • Output elements — Results of computation or analysis • Control mechanism — Comparison of actual with expected • Feedback system — Corrective action • Objectives — Expected/Ideal output

subjective.question: Discuss characteristics of Flat organization.
subjective.answer: Following are the characteristics of a flat organization: • High number of subordinates per supervisor • Short chain of command • Less number of levels • Eliminates middle level managers • Decentralizes authority to low level managers

subjective.question: How the chief executive is elected in any organization and what are his responsibilities?
subjective.answer: Chief executive is the highest-ranking corporate officer (executive) or administrator in charge of total management of an organization. An individual appointed as a CEO of a corporation, company, organization, or agency typically reports to the board of directors. The responsibility of a chief executive officer is to align the company, internally and externally, with his or her strategic vision. The core duty of a CEO is to facilitate business outside of the company while guiding employees and other executive officers towards a central objective.

subjective.question: Discuss the attributes on which Organizational Information Requirements depends.
subjective.answer: Organizations have various attributes which distinguish them from each other. No two organizations are similar in all respects. There have to be certain distinctive lines keeping them unique from each other. Information requirements keep varying in accordance with: • Size of organization • Its structure • The Culture it follows • Decision Making Structures • Interested parties both internal and external An organization should consider the above mentioned requirements while devising a system which tailors for specific information needs.

subjective.question: What are the management styles? Discuss in detail.
subjective.answer: Various management styles can be employed dependent on the culture of the business, the nature of the task, the nature of the workforce and the personality and skills of the leaders. There are three Management Styles: 1. Authoritative — An Autocratic or authoritarian manager makes all the decisions, keeping the information and decision making among the senior management. 2. Participative — In a Democratic style, the manager allows the employees to take part in decision making; therefore everything is agreed by the majority. The communication is extensive in both directions. This style can be particularly useful when complex decisions need to be made that require a range of specialist skills. 3. Mixed — This approach is a combination of both above styles. Input is taken and respected, final decision is taken by the senior management keeping in view the views given by the employees.

subjective.question: Enlist the types of models used in DSS.
subjective.answer: Types of Models Used in DSS: • Physical Models • Narrative Models • Graphic Models • Mathematical Models

subjective.question: Differentiate MIS from DSS.
subjective.answer: MIS: 1. Provides information on monitoring and controlling the business. 2. Fixed and regular reports are generated from data kept in TPS. 3. Report formats are predefined. 4. User is part of the system. 5. Controlled by IT Dept. DSS: 1. Helps in non routine decision making. 2. Users are not linked with the structured information flows. 3. Greater emphasis on models, display graphics & ad hoc queries. 4. DSS is a small part of users' actions. 5. Directly used by middle level managers.

subjective.question: What do you understand by Rational-Man Model?
subjective.answer: • In a rigorous rational model, it is presumed that the individual is rational enough to accurately rank all the alternatives. • However, in the real world of humans, specifying all of the alternatives and consequences is impossible. • Information systems based on this model need to be based on availability of perfect and complete information on all alternatives so as to ensure certainty. • Real life situations need to be given room for chances which this model does not provide for. Example: In a pharmaceutical drug company, the preparation and testing of life saving drug is a critical phase, and choice of a perfect alternative is inevitable. Hence the information system devised to support it should be such that it can record and monitor even the slightest variations. In an ammunitions factory, the testing and quality control of various bullets, shells, missiles, bombs, etc. is a sensitive issue. Since chances of error are quite high, the system from selecting and discarding should be with high sensitivity level.

subjective.question: Differentiate between Empire Building and Garbage Can Model.
subjective.answer: Empire Building: Empire building is a business term that refers to a common problem in larger organizations, in which managers attempt to gather more administrative and financial power. Power can only be shared in an organization with key employees in terms of their responsibilities & functions. Such employees are the key players in the decision making process. Hence decisions taken in an organization are a result of collective efforts of the leaders involved. This model is also termed as Political Model. Garbage Can Model: This model states that organizations are not rational. Decisions made are largely on accidental basis. Hence wrong solutions may be applied to wrong problems in an organization and critical mistakes may occur. Information systems should be designed to support and assist in relevant decision making, instead of making unrelated and wrong decisions.

subjective.question: What are the components of the Expert System and how they are different from the neural network?
subjective.answer: There are four main components of Expert systems: • User Interface: to enable the manager to enter instructions and information into an expert system to receive information from it. • Knowledge Base: it is the database of the expert system. It contains rules to express the logic of the problem. • Inference engine: it performs reasoning by using the contents of the knowledge base. • Development engine: it is used to create an expert system. Neural Network vs Expert System: Expert systems seek to model a human expert's way of solving problems. They are highly specific to seeking solutions. Neural networks do not model human intelligence. They seek to put intelligence into the hardware in the form of generalized capability to learn.

subjective.question: Discuss the concept of Knowledge/Intelligent Systems. Also discuss who are they built for and what are they built for?
subjective.answer: The set of processes developed in an organization to create, gather, store, maintain and apply the firm's knowledge is called Knowledge Management. Hence the systems that aid in the creation and integration of new knowledge in the organization are called knowledge systems. Who are they built for? This refers to defining the knowledge workers for whom the knowledge system is being built. The term refers to people who design products and services and create knowledge for an organization, for instance Engineers, Architects, Scientists. Knowledge systems are specially designed in assisting these professionals in managing the knowledge in an organization. What are they built for? Every knowledge system is built to maintain a specific form of knowledge. Hence it needs to be defined in the start, what the system would maintain. There are major types of knowledge: • Explicit knowledge — Structured internal knowledge e.g. product manuals, research reports, etc. • External knowledge of competitors, products and markets • Tacit knowledge — informal internal knowledge, which resides in the minds of the employees but has not been documented in structured form. Knowledge systems promote organizational learning by identifying, capturing and distributing these forms of knowledge.

subjective.question: Define MIS.
subjective.answer: Management Information System makes information available to relevant users by producing pre-determined and pre-designed reports required by the management. Management information system helps middle level management in planning, controlling and decision making. The data stored can be used or manipulated to produce differently defined reports from pre-defined reports. It can be presented graphically or pictorially. The reports generated by the MIS are used for analytical decision making by the management.

subjective.question: What do you understand by ESS?
subjective.answer: Executive Support System (ESS) is a reporting means that allow you to turn your organization's data into useful summarize reports. These reports are usually used by executive level managers for quick right of entry to reports coming from all company levels and sections such as billing, cost accounting, recruitment, preparation etc.

subjective.question: What is an Office Automation System?
subjective.answer: Office automation system includes formal and informal electronic systems primarily concerned with the communication of information to and from persons both inside and outside the firm. It supports data workers in an organization.

subjective.question: What is the purpose of Transaction Processing System?
subjective.answer: This system is used to record transactions of routine and repetitive nature. For instance: • Defining the transaction recording structure • Placing customer orders • Billing customers • Other basic business transactions Transaction processing is designed to maintain a computer system (typically a database or some modern file systems) in a known, consistent state, by ensuring that any operations carried out on the system that are interdependent are either all completed successfully or all canceled successfully.

subjective.question: What is the need for accounting information system (AIS) to be linked to all the information systems in an organization?
subjective.answer: Accounting information system is linked to all the information systems in an organization. This is important because the data required for proper book keeping and generation of transactional reports is extracted from all over the organization. For instance sales information can be sought only from marketing information system and stock information is available in manufacturing information system. The purpose of AIS is to accumulate data and provide decision makers (investors, creditors, and managers) with information to make decision.

subjective.question: What are the information requirements for Strategic level in Accounting & Financial Information Systems?
subjective.answer: Strategic level: 1. Investment goals 2. Long range forecasts for firm's financial performance 3. Acquisition of financial resources and goals

subjective.question: What are the information requirements for Management level in Accounting & Financial Information Systems?
subjective.answer: Management level: 1. Control over firm's financial resources 2. Investment management 3. Budget management 4. Tax management 5. Profitability & Performance Evaluation

subjective.question: What are the information requirements for operational level in Accounting & Financial Information Systems?
subjective.answer: Operational Level Requirements in Accounting & Financial Information Systems: 1. Cash flow statements through various transactions 2. Inventory and debtor's management 3. Creditors Management

subjective.question: Discuss information requirements at different levels of Management in Marketing Information System.
subjective.answer: MKIS should cater for information requirements at each level, for instance: Strategic Level: 1. Formulation of new sales products, and identifying new sales opportunities 2. Planning support for new products and services 3. Monitoring competitors Knowledge Level: 1. Market analysis based on demographics and customer behavior Management level: 1. Sales performance analysis is required to monitor how to enhance sales and address related issues. 2. Sales staff analysis is important to see how much of the sales portion has been contributed by each of the employees. Operational Level: 1. Taking comments from customers for measuring satisfaction 2. Tracking sales, processing orders and customer support

subjective.question: Discuss any five benefits of Marketing IS.
subjective.answer: MKIS helps organizations in efficient channel management. Following can be identified as some of the benefits of MKIS: 1. Customer profiles need to be maintained focusing on their habits and spending patterns. MKIS helps in maintaining these profiles. 2. Information on what competitors have been up to is also critical marketing information. This should not be taken as espionage on competitors. 3. Forecasts of demand are also a critical part of marketing analysis. MKIS helps in achieving this as well. 4. Field sales can also be monitored where sales agents are used to market products. 5. Customers can be quickly updated based on their information kept in MKIS. 6. Dealers involved in sale of product can also be monitored to help enhance revenue's.

subjective.question: List any three benefits of CRM.
subjective.answer: Benefits of CRM: • Maintains and enhances customer base • Encourages customer loyalty • Gaining more customers' wallet-share • The more effective a company's customer retention and defection management strategy, the less they need to plug the gap with new customers, who are expensive to recruit. • CRM helps in establishing communication to encourage customers to share information about their habits, tastes and preferences, and interests in company's brand extension initiatives.

subjective.question: Differentiate between Computer Aided Design and Computer Aided Manufacturing.
subjective.answer: Computer Aided Design (CAD): "It is a system that enables drawings to be constructed on a computer screen and subsequently stored, manipulated and updated electronically." Computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) is a form of automation where computers communicate work instructions directly to the manufacturing machinery.

subjective.question: Define basic goals of Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM).
subjective.answer: CIM has three basic goals: 1. Simplification of all manufacturing technologies and techniques 2. Automation of as many of the manufacturing processes as possible by integration of many information technologies like Flexible Manufacturing Systems (a form of flexible automation in which several machine tools are linked together by a material-handling system controlled by a central computer), Computer Aided Engineering (CAE — the application of computer software in engineering to analyze the robustness and performance of components, assemblies, products and manufacturing tools) and Just in Time (JIT — a Japanese idea that inventory is manufactured (or acquired) only as the need for it arises or in time to be sold (or used); a major goal is to cut down on inventory investment) 3. Integration and coordination of all the manufacturing aspects through computer hardware and software

subjective.question: What is the objective of MRP?
subjective.answer: Material procurement needs to be planned in compliance with the production Schedule. Materials Requirements Planning (MRP) is software based production planning and inventory control system for material procurement and scheduling. It helps in meeting three objectives: • Ensure materials and products are available for production and delivery to customers. • Maintain the lowest possible level of inventory. • Plan manufacturing activities, delivery schedules and purchasing activities. MRP helps in getting the right material and physical resources together at the right place and at the right time to meet the customer's requirements. This helps in achieving on time delivery, High Quality, at the best price.

subjective.question: List any two tools used in TQM.
subjective.answer: There are certain Graphical tools used to implement and promote TQM. For instance: • Histogram • Pareto Analysis • Cause & Effect Diagram

subjective.question: Discuss System Analysis in the light of the following points: 1. A technique to map the system under study. 2. To drill down into the various aspects of the business process without losing sight of the complete system.
subjective.answer: • System analysis helps to create an understanding of the business processes, their linkage with one another, the parameters governing the data flow within the business, the controls and checks built into the processes and the reporting needs in a business where a problem exists or for which the software needs to be designed. • System analysis creates the understanding and lays out the necessary relationships that will assist in defining a solution to the problem or the design of the proposed software that will meet the user needs.

subjective.question: Identify the basic purpose of DFD and identify the steps of designing a DFD for any process.
subjective.answer: A data flow diagram (DFD) is a graphical representation of the "flow" of data through an information system. The purpose of data flow diagrams is to provide a linking bridge between users and systems developers. Steps to draw a Data Flow Diagram: 1. Start from the context diagram. Identify the parent process and the external entities with their net inputs and outputs. 2. Place the external entities on the diagram. Draw the boundary. 3. Identify the data flows needed to generate the net inputs and outputs to the external entities. 4. Identify the business processes to perform the work needed to generate the input and output data flows. 5. Connect the data flows from the external entities to the processes. 6. Identify the data stores. 7. Connect the processes and data stores with data flows. 8. Apply the Process Model Paradigm to verify that the diagram addresses the processing needs of all external entities. 9. Apply the External Control Paradigm to further validate that the flows to the external entities are correct. 10. Continue to decompose to the nth level DFD. Draw all DFDs at one level before moving to the next level of decomposing detail.

subjective.question: What is the basic benefit of diagrammatic view of system?
subjective.answer: This helps to give a snapshot of what the entire system looks like. Various diagrammatic tools can be used while designing the system. User/Accountant uses chart of accounts to access the relevant accounts in order to prepare different vouchers according to requirements. The purpose behind this entire activity is to record various transactions.

subjective.question: What aspects should be covered by design of information flow?
subjective.answer: Design of the information flow is a major step in the conceptual design. Following aspects should be covered: • Flow of data & information and transformation points • The frequency and timing of flows • The extent of formality in these flows — input forms, report formats.

subjective.question: Designing file or database is a major component of system designing. Identify its basic purposes.
subjective.answer: Designing file or database serves following purposes: • Data accessibility is ensured to the user as and when required. • Data consistency — data updates in master file will automatically update the data in the whole system. • Data is efficiently processed & stored. • Data integrity, that is correctness of data, is ensured.

subjective.question: Various considerations need to be kept in mind while defining parameters for desired output in system designing. What should be them? Identify any three.
subjective.answer: Various considerations need to be kept in mind while defining parameters for desired output. These should generally focus on: • Assuring purposeful output • Providing output as defined and required by users • Providing appropriate information • Assuring distribution of output as per client specified requirements • Minimizing throughput time and Query time • Ensuring that output is available in client required mode

subjective.question: Discuss the purpose of Feasibility Study? Discuss key areas?
subjective.answer: Feasibility studies aim to objectively and rationally uncover the strengths and weaknesses of the existing business or proposed venture, opportunities and threats as presented by the environment, the resources required to carry through, and ultimately the prospects for success. Key Areas of Feasibility: • Technical Feasibility — is the available technology sufficient to support the proposed project? Can the technology be acquired or developed? (Response times, volume of transactions which can be processed within the given time, capacity to hold files or records of a certain size, number of users supported) • Operational Feasibility — compliance and adjustability with the way organization works with attitude to change or chains of command. Can the input data be collected for the system? Is the output usable? • Economic feasibility — Do the benefits of the system exceed the costs? It should be the BEST OPTION among those under consideration for the same purpose. • Behavioral feasibility — What impact will the system have on the user's quality of working life? Reduction in job stress, job satisfaction, quality of output by employees.

subjective.question: Define Technical Feasibility?
subjective.answer: Technical Feasibility — is the available technology sufficient to support the proposed project? Can the technology be acquired or developed? • Response times — time between request and execution • Volume of transactions, which can processed within the given time • Capacity to hold files or records of a certain size • Number of users supported

subjective.question: Identify different phases of Spiral model.
subjective.answer: There are usually four distinct phases of the spiral model software development approach: 1. Determine objectives, alternatives, constraints. 2. Evaluate alternatives, identify and resolve risks — This involves Risk analysis and Prototyping 3. Develop, verify next-level product 4. Plan next phase

subjective.question: Identify the Characteristics of the Incremental Model.
subjective.answer: Characteristics of the Incremental Model: • The system development is broken into many mini development projects • Partial systems are successively built to produce a final total system. • Highest priority requirements tackled early on. • Once an incremented portion is developed, requirements for that increment are frozen.

subjective.question: Differentiate between Incremental and iterative models with the help of one example each.
subjective.answer: Incremental vs. Iterative: These sound similar, and sometimes are equated but there is a subtle difference: • Incremental: add to the product at each phase • Iterative: re-do the product at each phase Example — Building a House: • Incremental: Starts with a modest house, keep adding rooms and upgrades to it. • Iterative: The design/construction map of the house is amended and improved and repeated until all the requirements are fulfilled.

subjective.question: Why prototypes are used?
subjective.answer: In many fields, there is great uncertainty as to whether a new design will actually do what is desired. New designs often have unexpected problems. A prototype is built to test the function of the new design before starting production of a product. Building the full design is often expensive and can be time-consuming. A prototype allows manufacturers to rapidly and inexpensively test the parts of the design that are most likely to have problems, solve those problems, and then build the full design.
